During a live broadcast on X late last month, Alex Jones
[declared](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5996424-alex-jones-
trump-impeachment-iran/) that "[t]he big issue" right now is "how to stop
Trump." "I mean," he quipped, "this is absolutely out of control." Jones
invoked the "25th Amendment, impeachment, whatever needs to happen . . . to
get control over the country." Congressional Democrats should take note.

Jones, the former owner of the right-wing conspiracy outlet InfoWars, is
incensed over Trump's illegal war in Iran, which, according to White House
press secretary Karoline Leavitt, could ultimately involve a draft. "They want
us in a total war so they can censor and take our freedoms, nationalize
everything, and push us aside with AI -- total liability, immunity, and
protection. This is a disaster. We are facing tyranny," Jones said. "We've got
to come together and transcend left and right, and we have to say no to an
expanded war that will definitely destroy the economy and kill a bunch of our
troops. They're preparing a massive ground invasion. It's all confirmed. This
is going down right now."

Jones hardly deserves applause for his comments, but his reveal is remarkable
- not only because he is a longtime Trump ally who abetted his return to the
White House, but because serious talk of Trump's impeachment has been mostly
"crickets," even among Democrats. In June, House Minority Leader Hakeem
Jeffries (D-N.Y.) [told](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/jeffries-trump-
impeachment.html) CNBC's Emily Wilkins that despite his optimism that the
party would take the House in November, it's not focused on impeachment, at
least "at this moment." "We haven't ruled anything in; we haven't ruled
anything out," he said.

If the populace does deliver Democrats a victory in either or both chambers
come November, Jeffries's tune had better change. Trump's approval ratings
have never been lower, with 73% of U.S. adults in a new [CNN
poll](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/29/politics/cnn-poll-donald-trump-midterms-
polls-iran-war) agreeing that he hasn't paid enough attention to the country's
most important problems. Overall, his [approval is at
33%](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-approval-falls-33-lowest-his-
presidency-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-08-17/). A Democratic win would
constitute a clear mandate that the American people demand accountability for
the overwhelming illegality, destruction, and corruption of this
administration.

Although some will argue that addressing the "affordability crisis" should be
Democrats' top priority, that would be missing the forest for the trees.
Without a functioning Constitution and rule of law, legislative policy
preferences become optional. Trump has established that new baseline time and
again, ignoring constitutional and statutory mandates with impunity. Americans
are feeling helpless and overwhelmed as a result. If voters tell Democrats to
do something about the carnage, they must act on day one.
